document_title: Support ticket routing with CRM sync
subtitle: A short plan to classify tickets, route them safely and write clean records back to your CRM.
job_title: Build an AI-Powered Customer Support Workflow with CRM Integration

items: Your agents read each ticket, pick a category and copy the details into the CRM by hand. This slows first response and makes routing inconsistent.

The goal is a workflow that suggests a category for each incoming request, sends it to the right team and writes a clean activity record to the CRM. Success means faster first response, fewer misrouted tickets and a measured accuracy baseline before automation acts on its own.

items.title: Review the real queue
items.description: We go through 100–200 past tickets together, agree the categories that matter and list the CRM fields agents actually use.

items.title: Agree the rules
items.description: We set confidence thresholds, human review for uncertain tickets, duplicate handling and the exact record written to the CRM.

items.title: Pilot in shadow mode
items.description: The model suggests categories on live tickets for two weeks. Your team compares its choices with theirs before routing is switched on.

items.title: Harden and hand over
items.description: I add retries, logs and monitoring, then write a short guide on changing categories and checking a bad classification.

items: An agreed category list, routing rules and confidence thresholds
A working connector for one channel, with CRM activity and contact sync
A shadow-mode report showing accuracy, false routes and sample failures
A short operator guide covering retries, escalations and rollback
Two review sessions with your team and a final handover walkthrough

rows.label: Working basis
rows.value: Fixed milestones with written acceptance criteria

rows.label: First milestone
rows.value: Category list and integration map in week one

rows.label: Indicative investment
rows.value: USD 4,800–6,200, confirmed after a short scoping call

rows.label: What I need from you
rows.value: Ticket samples, CRM sandbox access and one support lead for reviews

items: Can you connect to our CRM and helpdesk? Yes. Tell me the platforms and versions and I will check their APIs before the first milestone.
Can customer data stay private? Yes. The pilot can use a redacted payload or a local classifier, and we agree the data policy before any live traffic.
What accuracy do you target? At least 90% agreement with your team on the top five categories, with every low-confidence ticket sent to a person.

items.title: 15-minute call
items.description: We confirm the queue, the CRM and the channel for the pilot.

items.title: Scoping note
items.description: I send a one-page scope, milestone plan and fixed price within two working days.

items.title: Kickoff
items.description: We start with ticket samples and the integration map once the scope is signed off.

closing: Thank you for reading. I am happy to walk through the plan or adjust the pilot scope on a short call.
